main.description: Records a funding receipt for a payment from one user to another user. It may be recorded by the recipient, by the sender, or by a third party. The sender may remain anonymous.

from.description: The sender of the funds (a free-text string, an account DID, or a strong reference to a record). Optional — omit to represent anonymity.

to.description: The recipient of the funds (a free-text string, an account DID, or a strong reference to a record).

amount.description: Amount of funding received as a numeric string (e.g. '1000.50').

currency.description: Currency of the payment (e.g. EUR, USD, ETH).

fx.description: Optional foreign-exchange context. Stamp at payment time whenever amount/currency is not the denomination the payment was actually made in (e.g. a platform recording a USD-normalized amount for a EUR card payment or an on-chain transfer). Receipts for the same payment written by other parties should copy this block verbatim from the receipt they reference, so consumers comparing or aggregating receipts reconcile deterministically instead of re-deriving rates that drift over time.

paymentRail.description: How the funds were transferred (e.g. bank_transfer, credit_card, onchain, cash, check, payment_processor).

paymentNetwork.description: Optional network within the payment rail (e.g. arbitrum, ethereum, sepa, visa, paypal).

transactionId.description: Identifier of the underlying payment transaction (e.g. bank reference, onchain transaction hash, or processor-specific ID). Use paymentNetwork to specify the network where applicable. Receipts are published to public repositories, so choose identifiers accordingly: prefer opaque processor IDs (dereferenceable only by the processor and the account holder) or internal payment references; avoid bank references that embed account details; and note that an onchain transaction hash publicly reveals the sending wallet — when the sender is deliberately anonymous (from omitted), consider whether publishing the hash is appropriate.

for.description: Optional strong reference to the activity, project, or organization this funding relates to.

refundOf.description: Optional strong reference marking this receipt as a refund — partial or whole — of the referenced receipt. Receipts are immutable once published (attestations bind to their content), so refunds are represented as new receipts rather than edits: amount/currency carry the refunded amount in the same denomination as the original (copy the original's fx block so partial refunds are computed at the original rate, without forex drift); from/to mirror the original reversed (when the original sender was anonymous, use the #text party for the refund's recipient). Multiple partial refunds are multiple refund receipts. Consumers aggregating funding should net refund receipts against the receipt they reference.

notes.description: Optional notes or additional context for this funding receipt.

createdAt.description: Client-declared timestamp when this receipt record was created.

signatures.description: Optional cryptographic signatures attesting to this record's content.

text.description: A free-text string value (e.g. a display name, wallet address, or other identifier).

fxInfo.description: Foreign-exchange context binding a receipt's amount/currency to the payment's original denomination at a point in time.

originalAmount.description: Amount actually paid, as a numeric string, denominated in originalCurrency.

originalCurrency.description: Currency the payment was actually made in (e.g. EUR, CELO, USDC).

rate.description: Conversion rate applied at payment time, as a numeric string: the price of one unit of originalCurrency expressed in the receipt's currency, so amount = originalAmount x rate (up to rounding). Recording the rate explicitly removes rounding ambiguity and lets later computations (e.g. partial refunds) reuse the original rate instead of drifting with the market.

rateSource.description: Where the rate came from (e.g. stripe, ecb, coingecko).

rateTimestamp.description: When the rate was captured; usually the payment time.
